directorStatement.audienceFeeling: The audience laughs as one tiny rude raindrop starts tattling on Sunny’s perfect party, then feels the sting as every wet object proves she is smiling faster than she is feeling.
directorStatement.emotionalChange: Sunny owns the scene. Her want is control made visible through neatness; her need is the disappointment she refuses to feel. We stay close enough to notice the fraction-too-long smile and the one private droop before she rebounds.
directorStatement.theLaugh: Environmental participation plus escalating overcommitment. The clearing does not attack her; it simply refuses to stay arranged. Each fix creates a new visible loss: straight cups fill, garlands sag, lanterns hiss out.
directorStatement.visualSurprise: A low party-level view of perfectly straight berry cups beneath a gorgeous garland, Sunny’s paws making one final exact adjustment as warm clearing light catches her Citrine confidence. -> The same party world now wet and uneven: cups brimming, garland sagging, lantern dark, Sunny already lifting herself into motion with “New plan! We move the party inside!” while the bruise of the ruined setup remains in frame.
directorStatement.carryForward: Sunny drives the story indoors with a practical new plan while the ruined outdoor setup remains emotionally unresolved.

northStar.surfaceStory: Sunny’s perfect outdoor party setup is interrupted by rain, and she scrambles to save it by moving everything inside.
northStar.universalTruth: When you build your happiness around everything going exactly right, the first small mess can feel like it is exposing you, not just changing the plan.
northStar.childClearWant: Sunny wants the party decorations, cups, lanterns and weather to stay perfect.
northStar.emotionalNeed: She needs to let disappointment actually land instead of racing past it with a brighter new plan.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If I keep smiling and fixing fast enough, nothing is really ruined.
northStar.relationshipEngine: Sunny is performing joy for the friends she wants to delight; the imagined look on their faces makes every wet cup and drooping garland feel personal.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A child preparing something special can mistake neatness for love, then panic when ordinary weather makes their effort look messy.
northStar.sceneTurn: The first raindrop is a tiny contradiction; the sky opening turns Sunny’s cheerful control into frantic triage.
audienceJourney: pleased by Sunny’s tiny stage-manager pride
amused by the first drop puncturing her certainty
concerned as her smile starts working too hard
energised by her practical new plan while sensing she has not felt the disappointment yet
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Forward motion with a bruise underneath: Sunny has a plan, but the ache of the ruined outdoor party is still chasing her.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: Do not add any explanation of how Sunny feels. Her held smile, faster paws, tiny slump before rebounding, flickering Citrine and the rain-swamped party must carry the denial beneath the locked lines.
northStar.environmentPressure: Rain actively defeats Sunny’s proof of control: garlands sag, cups fill, lanterns hiss out, surfaces grow slippery, and every object she straightened becomes evidence that the world will not obey her plan.

creativeIntent.selectedTreatment: Combined treatment: “The Perfect Line Meets the First Plink” as the spine, “The Party Objects Tell on Her” as the scene’s evidentiary lens, and limited “Small Sunny, Big Sky” scale accents.
creativeIntent.governingAudienceExperience: The audience laughs as one tiny rude raindrop starts tattling on Sunny’s perfect party, then feels the sting as every wet object proves she is smiling faster than she is feeling.
creativeIntent.scenePurpose: Sunny’s perfectly arranged outdoor party is interrupted by rain, turning neat proof of control into wet evidence that she is outrunning disappointment.
creativeIntent.emotionalPointOfView: Sunny owns the scene. Her want is control made visible through neatness; her need is the disappointment she refuses to feel. We stay close enough to notice the fraction-too-long smile and the one private droop before she rebounds.
creativeIntent.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Environmental participation plus escalating overcommitment. The clearing does not attack her; it simply refuses to stay arranged. Each fix creates a new visible loss: straight cups fill, garlands sag, lanterns hiss out.
creativeIntent.characterPerformanceStrategy: Sunny begins as a tiny stage manager: brisk paws, satisfied checks, bright run-on certainty. After the first drop she over-brightens, trying to make luck out of contradiction. In the downpour her movement becomes triage: fast, practical, almost impressive, but emotionally evasive. The key turn is her brief slump before “New plan!”—the disappointment almost lands, then she outruns it.
creativeIntent.visualGrammar: Start with orderly horizontal and vertical lines: rows of cups, garland arcs, lantern spacing. Rain slowly bends the composition. The scene’s grammar is straight becoming drooped, dry sparkle becoming wet weight, warm gold interrupted by cool grey.
creativeIntent.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like Sunny’s helper at first, inspecting what she has arranged. When rain arrives, it stops cooperating and begins discovering damage slightly before or after she does, so her control feels unstable.
creativeIntent.movementVersusStillness: Early movement is precise and small. The first raindrop earns a still hold. The downpour becomes darting, interrupted motion. Sunny’s abrupt brief stillness before the final line is the emotional crack, not a pause for timing.
creativeIntent.depthAndEnvironment: Depth carries pressure: Sunny in the near plane trying to fix one object while, behind her, another decoration loses the fight. The sky stays present above the party without becoming threatening; it is simply larger than her plan.
creativeIntent.rhythmAndEscalation: Proud checklist, tiny plink, denial, second contradiction, sudden rain, frantic fixes, one small sag in Sunny, then a bright practical rebound. The rhythm should let children laugh at the wet party while adults feel the cost of her forced brightness.
creativeIntent.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by new contradictions: a drop, a filled cup, a lantern going out, Sunny noticing. Avoid automatic reaction coverage. Hold when Sunny is performing control; cut when the world proves something has changed.
creativeIntent.openingImage: A low party-level view of perfectly straight berry cups beneath a gorgeous garland, Sunny’s paws making one final exact adjustment as warm clearing light catches her Citrine confidence.
creativeIntent.closingImage: The same party world now wet and uneven: cups brimming, garland sagging, lantern dark, Sunny already lifting herself into motion with “New plan! We move the party inside!” while the bruise of the ruined setup remains in frame.
creativeIntent.handoverToNextScene: Sunny drives the story indoors with a practical new plan while the ruined outdoor setup remains emotionally unresolved.
creativeIntent.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, splashy relief with the ache still visible in the rain and the soggy crown.

inputs.title: Perfectly Rainy
inputs.logline: Sunny tries to save her flawless outdoor party from the rain, but only finds real joy when she stops performing sunshine and lets her friends turn the mess into the party.

orderedEvents.text: A golden HONEYCOMB hangs from a branch. KEEN has built a catapult from sticks and a bendy branch. He loads a BERRY. Steps back. One eye closed. Tongue out. He lines up the shot — aiming carefully at the honeycomb. Nearby — ZENNY sits cross-legged on a leaf. Zenny meditates. Keen fires. WHOOSH — the berry flies — SPLAT. Right onto Zenny’s forehead. Juice slowly drips down. Keen ducks for cover and hides. Zenny’s eye twitches. She opens her eyes. Looks around. Sees — FUZZBY asleep on the honeycomb. Fuzzby snores, then awakens, laughing at Zenny. Zenny calmly licks the berry juice from her face. Closes her eyes again.

orderedEvents.speaker: Zenny
orderedEvents.text: OK, Fuzzby, calm down. It’s not that funny.
Above — Fuzzby is laughing so much that Keen sees an opportunity.

beats.storyBeat: Keen’s over-careful catapult plan misfires onto the one character least interested in chaos. The joke belongs to Zenny’s restraint and Fuzzby’s delighted lack of restraint, while Keen hides from the consequence he caused.
beats.want: Keen wants to pull off a clever honeycomb shot without being caught.
beats.need: He needs to learn that bold action still has consequences other people feel.
beats.kidRead: A berry splats the wrong bee and the calm bee gets juice on her face.
beats.adultRead: A child’s private mischief becomes funny because the wrong witness absorbs it with heroic restraint.
beats.emotionalIntent: Open with safe, character-specific mischief and establish imperfection as playable, not dangerous.
